about.text: Arkhi distilled a second time, stronger than the first, at around 30 % alcohol: in Mongolian, arz.

links.name: Bianquis, Les alcools de lait en Mongolie (OCHA, 2004)

how.text: The heritage text describes the first distillation of fermented milk as arz; other sources here call arz the second distillation of arkhi. The source gives no temperatures or strength for further rounds.

links.name: National Center for Cultural Heritage (Mongolia): The traditional technique of distilling milk alcohol (Shimiin arkhi)

steps.name: distil
steps.note: The cooling water is changed 2–4 times per run, depending on how far the milk has fermented, and half of the top-pot water is replaced with cold when it boils.

facts.v: The first alcohol out is stronger and is called 'essence'
More water changes give more spirit but a weaker taste, sometimes called 'suvs' (weak)
